newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes off, ANS standoff foreseen.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes off, ANS standoff foreseen.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes lost ground Friday in quiet post-holiday talk tracking action on NYMEX, but players expect the market to grow lively next week ahead of several refinery maintenance projects, traders said.

Some traders said the fulcrum of price discussions in Alaskan North Slope (ANS) markets was likely to be Exxon, which they say has maintenance planned soon at its Benicia, California refinery east of San Francisco.
"We're going to see a lot of shutdowns in February, including Exxon which runs over 100,000 barrels a day of ANS," said one trader who saw downward pressure on ANS diffs.
He weighed in with an ANS bid of $2.25 under the West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, the same as the average bid.
But another trader more focused on selling the bellwhether West Coast grade, said he expected diffs to hold their levels, and weighed in with an above-market ANS offer of $1.50 under WTI/Cushing.
"Exxon may kick some ANS out, and we'll respond appropriately," the trader said, noting he did not think the maintenance projects would appreciably weaken ANS diffs.
But other traders saw the weakness extending to other grades, such as those in the San Joaquin Valley like Kern River crude.
Some said offers on the Kern River grade had already slipped by 15 cents to 25 cents under posted prices, though offers were hanging tough at the price of posted prices.
Traders said the diff drama would likely begin playing out beginning next week when traders return from their holidays and moribund markets come out of their recent slumber.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1633
